THE HUMAN ATLASES · DEEP DIVE

South Asian, East Asian & Pacific Origin Stories: Vedic Hymns, Pangu & Nüwa, Kojiki, Dangun & Polynesian Cosmogonies

Across Asia and the vast islands of the Pacific, religious scriptures and oral genealogical chants frame origins not around a single linear event, but through cosmic eggs, golden embryos, divine sacrifice, clay-fashioning goddesses, imperial descent islands, and the wrenching separation of Sky and Earth.

Primary sacred and classical literary traditions spanning Vedic/Hindu, Buddhist, Jain, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Māori, Hawaiian, and Samoan–Tongan cosmogonies.

1. South Asian Cosmogonies: Rigvedic Wonder, Brahma's Cosmic Egg & the Aggañña Sutta

South Asian traditions begin not with a single orthodoxy, but with audacious philosophical questioning. Rigveda 10.129—the celebrated *Nāsadīya Sūkta* ('Hymn of Creation')—opens before existence or non-existence, when breath breathed windless by itself inside undifferentiated waters, ending by asking whether even the highest seer in heaven truly knows how creation arose. Alongside it, *Hiraṇyagarbha* imagines a primordial Golden Embryo floating on cosmic waters, the *Puruṣa Sūkta* (Rigveda 10.90) tells how cosmic sacrifice divided the thousand-headed Cosmic Person into sun, moon, wind, and the human social orders, and later *Purāṇas* weave Brahma emerging upon a lotus from sleeping Vishnu's navel to set cyclical *yugas* and *Manvantaras* turning around successive first sages (*Manu*). [1] [4]

Diverging sharply from creator-god theology, Jain cosmology holds the universe (*loka*) to be uncreated and eternal, turning endlessly like a six-spoked wheel between ascending (*utsarpini*) and descending (*avasarpini*) eras—while the early Buddhist *Aggañña Sutta* (Dīgha Nikāya 27) offers a famous playful parable in which luminous self-radiant mind-made beings drift down into a freshly coalesced earth-film; tasting savory earth crust out of curiosity and greed coarsens their bodies into physical flesh, dims cosmic light until sun and moon appear, introduces private rice fields, and leads villagers to elect the first 'Great Elect' (*Mahāsammata*) king to keep peace. [4]

2. East Asian Creations: Pangu & Nüwa (China), Hwanung & Dangun (Korea), Izanagi & Izanami (Japan)

Early Chinese cosmology blended philosophical *Daoist* emergence—where the nameless Dao generates One, Two (Yin and Yang), Three, and the Ten Thousand Things—with vivid mythological narratives recorded from Han and Three Kingdoms texts (including Xu Zheng's *Sanwu Liji* and earlier Han stone reliefs). Inside cosmic chaos shaped like a hen's egg (*Hundun*), horned giant **Pangu** grew for 18,000 years until his axe cracked Yang sky upward and Yin earth downward; pushing them apart daily for another 18,000 years, his dying body became wind, thunder, sun and moon (his eyes), five sacred mountains, rivers (veins), and soil. Afterward, half-serpent Goddess **Nüwa** walked the silent empty world and kneaded glowing yellow river-mud with her fingers—creating noble forms carefully one by one, then flicking droplets off a dipped reed-rope across the bank when her hands grew tired, peopling Earth before patching the broken sky-pillar with five-colored melted stones. [3] [1]

Across the Korean Peninsula (recorded in Iryeon's 13th-century *Samguk Yusa*), Sky-lord Hwanin's son **Hwanung** descended to a sacred sandalwood tree atop Mount Taebaek bringing winds, rain, clouds, agriculture, and 3,000 followers to govern humankind. When a bear and a tiger prayed to become human, Hwanung set both a hundred-day cave fast on wormwood and twenty cloves of garlic; the patient bear emerged transformed after twenty-one days as **Ungnyeo** ('Bear-Woman'), wed Hwanung, and bore **Dangun Wanggeom**, traditional founder of Gojoseon. In Japan's *Kojiki* (712 CE) and *Nihon Shoki* (720 CE), successive uncoupled generations of sky deities (*Kotoamatsukami*) gave way to **Izanagi** and **Izanami** standing atop *Ama-no-ukihashi* (the Floating Bridge of Heaven), dipping the jeweled spear *Ame-no-nuboko* into oily brine so falling salt drops solidified into Onogoro Island, giving birth to the Japanese islands, fire, mountains, and solar goddess **Amaterasu**. [1] [4]

3. Pacific Cosmogonies: Te Kore, Rangi & Papa, the Hawaiian Kumulipo & Tagaloa's Ocean World

Across Polynesia, oral genealogies (*whakapapa* / *moʻokūʻauhau*) bridge cosmic darkness directly to living islands and ancestors. In Māori tradition across Aotearoa, existence uncoiled out of **Te Kore** (pure undifferentiated potential) and aeons of **Te Pō** (the Great Night) into **Ranginui** (Sky Father) and **Papatūānuku** (Earth Mother), locked in tight, cold, shadowy embrace around their trapped divine sons. Pushing upward upside-down with shoulders on Earth and feet planted against Heaven, **Tāne-mahuta** (forest god) braced and rent his parents apart so light (**Te Ao Mārama**) poured onto Earth—later shaping **Hine-ahu-one**, the 'Earth-formed Maid,' out of sacred red clay at **Kurawaka** and breathing *tihei mauri ora* (the sneeze of life) into her nostrils. [2]

North in Hawai'i, the monumental 2,102-line **Kumulipo** creation chant opens inside *Lipo* (unfathomable blackness) as coral polyps emerge alongside matching land plants, sea creatures, birds, mammals, and stars—descending to **Papa** and **Wākea** and their stillborn child **Hāloa-naka**, out of whose burial grew the first **kalo** (taro) plant sustaining the living elder-sibling covenant between Hawaiian humanity (**Hāloa**) and the land. In Samoa and Tonga, sky-creator **Tagaloa-a-Lagi** rested atop primal rock **Manu'atele**, cast vines over emergent volcanic reef rocks, and shaped worm-like creatures inside decaying vine-leaves into the first thinking, speaking women and men. [2] [4]
